name: Curve+Credit Confluence Cyclical Tilt: long XLF/XLE/XLK when the 2s10s is steepening AND high-yield credit is tight
rationale: Thesis: the sector-rotation map is conditioned on TWO genuinely orthogonal macro axes JOINTLY, not on either alone. Cyclicals (XLF financials, XLE energy, XLK tech) lead in EARLY EXPANSION — when the 2s10s yield curve is STEEPENING (a positive CHANGE in slope widens bank net-interest margins and signals reflation) AND high-yield credit spreads are TIGHT (low default-risk premium, ample risk appetite). The regime ARMS a long cyclical tilt; it does not trade any single sector's own momentum. The defensive flip (late-cycle de-risking into utilities/staples) is captured here as the EXIT: when HY credit spreads cross UP (widening = risk-off de-risking) the cyclical regime is no longer confirmed and we step aside. Confluence design that avoids the level traps: yield_curve_2s10s is entered via cross_up (its STEEPENING change arms the trade — using the change rather than the raw level avoids the always-true/false slope trap), while credit_spread (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, the ICE BofA US High-Yield OAS in percent, ~3-10) must sit BELOW a fitted tight threshold. These two FRED series are economically distinct inputs (rate-curve term structure vs default-risk premium), so requiring BOTH to agree is a real second filter — NOT one axis dressed as two. (Deliberately NOT using macro_regime here: in the current data macro_regime is ingested from the SAME raw T10Y2Y series as yield_curve_2s10s, so adding it would be collinear with the curve leg and the 'confluence' would be a single signal in disguise — the very trap this hypothesis is built to test.) Disconfirmer 1: a CONTROL spec firing the SAME cyclical entry on curve-steepening ALONE (drop the credit_spread leg) — if it matches this confluence version, credit is dead weight and this collapses to an exhausted single-signal regime, FAIL. Disconfirmer 2: a CONTROL on credit-tight ALONE — same logic, if it matches, the curve cross is redundant. Disconfirmer 3: this rotation must beat a static equal-weight hold of the sector ETFs net of rebalance fees, and beat plain cross-sectional momentum among them (the leader could just be whichever sector already ran). Disconfirmer 4: the cyclical leg must NOT be merely long-XLE-when-oil-is-up — that would show as correlation to oil, not to the curve+credit confluence. Low-turnover by construction: entries fire only on the steepening cross while credit is already tight, and we exit on the credit-widening flip — respecting the equity ETF cost drag.
catalyst: 2s10s yield curve steepens (cross-up of slope) WHILE high-yield credit spreads are tight — early-expansion confluence arms the cyclical sector tilt
